steps.name: Summary: slim top bar (menu button left, flags right), five tabs at the bottom, all ten party cards in two columns
Party card: a tap highlights the party; the search-and-filters tab counts it; the House dims the others
Map: a full-screen map with nothing on top of a province; a tap opens a province above a panel; a constituency opens in the panel
Back button: constituency → province → map of Thailand → summary, instead of leaving the site
Focus + context: a finger held on the map opens a lens; the province under it and its neighbours grow, the rest of the country stays
Lens at the edges and with motion on: a province at the edge stays whole on screen; the lens swells and melts back without a trace
Colour key and colourings: the key opens over the map with the full credit and how the lens works; a sheet explains all five colourings
Search and filters share one panel: search on top (16 px, not focused, so the keyboard does not cover the filters), examples, then the filters
Menu: the button at the top left slides a drawer in from the left with the theme, the data status and the sources; five ways to close it
Analysis: one chart at a time; previous / next and a list of all eight charts with their questions
Analysis tap: the first tap opens the tooltip as a card above the tab bar; its button does what a click does
Finishing places: one bar per party; a tap on a part of a bar names it, and its button selects those constituencies
The House tab: the majority builder with who governs now; government and opposition as two cards; the analysis tab goes back to the chart before
Candidate records: ranked rows with photos; a row opens the constituency in a sheet that can be dragged down to close
Comparison: a search box and a province menu add constituencies; each fact is a block with the constituencies under one another
Small phones 360×780, 375×667 and 320×568: no sideways scrolling, five tabs that fit, panel and map share the screen, the lens works
Held sideways (844×390): the tabs become a rail on the left, the map sits beside its details, the lens and the drawer work
Phones held sideways wider than 900 px (932×430) still get the phone layout; a desktop window of the same size does not
Desktop keeps its layout (no lens, no drawer); a narrow window gets the phone layout, where a mouse drag opens the lens
